memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium (a Triaging-stage view, directional). Bank Pekao (PEO-PL) is a self-help case inside a good franchise, arriving after the market has paid for it: at PLN 276.5 (close 2026-10-06) the modal total shareholder return is about 4.6% a year over eighteen months and 9.1% a year over three years against the 20% bar, so the case is parked on return, not on quality. The park rule does not trigger: management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability B. Re-open below about PLN 210 to 225 (about PLN 225 on the eighteen-month path, PLN 208 on the three-year path, where the modal path returns 20% a year), or on a tabled PZU reorganisation bill with the exchange parity set, or on an FY2028 consensus earnings per share heading above about PLN 33. The record's judgement in one line: a well-run Polish bank whose next two years of earnings growth are a tax refund the market has already banked, priced at the top of its range by a sector-wide re-rating, with a 6% yield and a capital-release option that depends on legislation before an election.
case: - The thesis. Bank Pekao is a self-help case inside a good franchise, arriving after the market has paid for it. At PLN 276.5 the shares price a 3.6% to 3.7% net interest margin, a 34% cost ratio and a legislated tax refund at the top of the stock's own five-year range, so the modal return is about 4.6% a year over eighteen months and 9.1% a year over three years against the 20% bar; the same facts clear the bar only below about PLN 210 to 225.

- The change is internal and real; the dominant external force is a headwind on the largest revenue line. A proven private-sector operator was placed on Poland's second-largest bank by the 2024 political reset (the Tusk government's dismissals after the December 2023 election). Three of the framework's twelve internal forces are strong (the chief-executive change, a resourced strategy with hard targets, visible standards improvement: 500 voluntary redundancies, inflation-linked pay rises removed for middle and top management, thirteen branches closed in 2025, the PeoBIZ 2.0 migration completed 2026-01-01, a special audit of the former board with bonuses and discharge denied), a fourth is mooted (the capital release), and the margin-defence actions (fixed-rate mortgages at 90% of new production and 40% of the book, PLN 49,559m of cash-flow hedges at end-2025, a lowered margin sensitivity) make "the margin has bottomed at 3.65%" plausible rather than hopeful. Against this, Polish policy rates fell 200 basis points to 3.75%, the net interest margin (about 75% of operating revenue) fell from 4.2% in FY2025 to 3.65% in Q2 2026, the bank tax rate rose from 19% to 30%, and fines, a court ruling and higher levies landed in the same year. Demand is the tailwind: GDP +3.9%, corporate loans +14%, cash loans +14.8%, Credit Information Bureau loan sales +31%. Net: 'Change Forces' C, with external forces C and internal forces B; the screen rule is met on the count of forces but not on the second route, because guidance was reiterated, not raised, and 1H 2026 return on equity of 15.7% to 16.0% is short of the above-18% target.

- 'Financial Outputs' have reached the operating metrics and the sell-side's outer years, not earnings per share. The cost-to-income ratio excluding the Bank Guarantee Fund held at 34.0% in 1H 2026 through a 12% rise in other administrative costs and double-digit IT depreciation; fees grew 11%; cash-loan sales were a record. But 1H 2026 net profit fell 16% on the tax step, FY2026 consensus earnings per share of PLN 22.77 are 15% below FY2025's PLN 26.73, and the operating margin read as the pre-provision margin has drifted from about 67% to about 65.5% and is being held, not lifted. The sell-side raised FY2027 and FY2028 estimates by 4.2% and 5.8% over three months and FY2028 by 10.6% over six, after cuts in the twelve months to spring 2026; most of the 20% six-month target-price move was multiple (Morgan Stanley's cost of equity to 11% from 12%), not earnings (+8%). Upgrades ahead are plausible but modest: the drivers of the recent upgrades (lower costs, lower Bank Guarantee Fund fees, a lower cost of equity) are in the numbers; the next move needs a shallower rate path or proof the cost ratio holds through the IT catch-up. The record's own FY2026 and FY2027 (PLN 22.8 and 25.8) sit on or 2% below consensus, near the low end of the brokers' range (PLN 25.19 to 27.20 for FY2027).
counter_case: The strongest case against the park, at full force, as the record carried it: Pekao is a bank earning a 16% to 18% return on equity with a 6% yield, earnings per share growing 13% a year for two years, a cost ratio proven through an investment cycle (34.0% excluding the Bank Guarantee Fund while IT costs rise double digits), the lowest deposit beta (36%) and the best Swiss-franc coverage (211%) in Poland, a chief executive with the best record in the sector (a 27% cost ratio and a 40% core return on equity at mBank), volumes growing double digits in the right segments, a margin that has bottomed at 3.65%, a tax rate falling 7 points over two years, a 75% payout, and a PLN 15bn to 20bn capital release (21% to 28% of the PLN 72.6bn market capitalisation) that no broker models. It trades at a 6% discount to Polish peers (PKO-PL 10.4x, MBK-PL 11.5x, ING-PL 11.8x) and at about 2.0x book against a sector that has re-rated for structural reasons (higher rates for longer, fiscal expansion, EU funds); Morgan Stanley's bull case is PLN 355, which from PLN 276.5 with one dividend is about 21% a year over eighteen months. On this view the correct multiple is PKO-PL's 10.4x or better, the setup is a 'Compounder' at B whose mis-modelled line is the whole of 2027 and 2028, and the correct rating is a B rather than a park. Against the 'Foundations' B, the counter-case (the leadership digest's "medium plausibility" and the risks digest's state-control argument) is that a bank whose board is appointed by the political cycle, whose directors hold no shares, whose profits are taxed at 30% and whose products are regulated by the UOKiK, the CJEU and the Sejm does not own its outputs, so its foundations are less robust than its ratios suggest. Against the 'Investment Case' D, the counter-case is that the record penalises the stock twice for its price, once in the return and again in mark-to-market and mediocrity, when the business and the management are B.

The record's response, and where it concedes. It concedes every operating fact, the yield, the relative discount to Polish peers, the option value of the release, the tax line, that the state is both owner and tax-setter and caps the business at B, and the double-counting overlap (stated once in the Written Summary). It holds for three reasons the bull must answer. First, the 13% is measured from a trough the tax step itself created; from FY2025 reported earnings per share compound at 2.9% a year to FY2028 (26.73 to 29.1), and the bull's own consensus path (28.90) is no different; once the step-down is complete in FY2028 the growth rate falls to the mid-single digits that a 3.6% margin, 8% volume growth and a sub-35% cost ratio produce, and 9.78x already discounts that path. Second, on the bull's own numbers, consensus earnings and a held 9.78x, the three-year return is 11.7% a year (a D), at PKO-PL's 10.4x about 13.6% (a C); the bull reaches 20% only at about 12.6x, the ten-year 90th percentile, or with FY2028 earnings per share near PLN 36, 25% above consensus. Third, the release accrues to a merged entity at a parity not yet set, through legislation not yet passed, with the minister examining alternatives; at 38% odds and PLN 57 to 76 a share gross, its expected value is PLN 22 to 29 a share, about 8% to 10% of the price, lifting the three-year rate by roughly 3 points if all of it reached Pekao's holders, to about 12% a year, still a D. On the 'Compounder' claim: the framework's 'Compounder' is a proven upgrader over many years, and Pekao's earnings per share were PLN 25.37, 24.29 and 26.73 for FY2023 to FY2025, flat for three years at the peak of the rate cycle; the sell-side's twelve-month moves are a recovery from cuts, not a compounding upgrade. On the 'Foundations': the foundations the thesis needs (the deposit franchise, corporate relationships, capital, provisioning, cost discipline) are demonstrably in place and survived two political resets and PLN 1,900m of credit holidays; the state risk is a risk to the 'Investment Case', rated there. On the 'Investment Case': Building Block 4 asks whether the whole case is robust to being wrong, and at PLN 276.5 it has little margin for the three things most likely to go wrong (a faster rate path, a political intervention, a sector de-rating), each of the sudden shape and none controlled by management. The response does not change the rating; it fixes the level at which the record would change it.
triggers: - Re-open levels: about PLN 225 on the eighteen-month path and PLN 208 on the three-year path (the record also says "below about PLN 210 to 225" and "below about PLN 220"); or an FY2028 consensus earnings per share heading above about PLN 33; or a reorganisation structure that puts the capital release in Pekao shareholders' hands at a parity set.

- Net interest margin ('Case/SP Key Driver'): modal hold at 3.6% to 3.7% through 2027, probable about 65%; alarm below 3.55% in any quarter or a cut before April 2027; invalidate below 3.4% or an NBP rate below 3.0%. Tested first at the Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-29.

- Cost-to-income ratio excluding the Bank Guarantee Fund ('Case/SP Key Driver'): modal hold at 33% to 35%, probable about 70%; alarm above 35.5% in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027; invalidate above 36% (the earnings review's own trigger).

- Bank tax rate ('Case/SP Key Driver'): modal step to 26% on 1 January 2027 and 23% in 2028, probable about 70%; alarm any bill to freeze at 30% or add a levy; invalidate the statutory rate not stepping down on 1 January 2027. Consensus implies 31.5% effective in FY2027 and 29.5% in FY2028, so the market already carries a haircut.
- Payout ('Case/SP Key Driver'): modal 70%; alarm a proposal below 60%; invalidate below 50% or a KNF cap. Consensus FY2026 dividend PLN 16.96.

- Policy rates ('Case/SP Key Risk'): modal hold to the 2027-04-16 NBP meeting, then 50 basis points to 3.25%; alarm a cut before April 2027; invalidate a cut of more than 50 basis points in one meeting or a terminal rate below 3.0%.
